overview: This 474-page file traces Japanese naval and public vessel visits to U.S. ports from 1930 to 1936. Diplomatic and interdepartmental records document reciprocal notification rules, port courtesies, tanker visits, and disputes over unannounced arrivals. Reports and Panama newspaper clippings show how the 1933 training squadron’s reception intersected with espionage allegations and criticism of Japan’s actions in China.
interest: The file pairs routine port diplomacy with Panama press controversy and detailed disputes over Japanese vessels’ arrival dates.
